query: For lightweight high-entropy alloys intended for weight-sensitive aerospace and rail-transportation applications, what single, testable intervention hypothesis could improve mechanical performance, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance while retaining low density? Specify the intervention, the proposed causal mechanism, the predicted outcomes relative to an unmodified lightweight-high-entropy-alloy baseline, the conditions under which the hypothesis should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and a controlled experiment with clear results that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of refractory metals such as Hf and Mo to a lightweight high-entropy alloy can improve its mechanical performance, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance while retaining low density.
generation.intervention: Addition of refractory metals such as Hf and Mo
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a single BCC solid solution, precipitation of coherent nanoprecipitations
generation.mechanism: The refractory metals can enhance the strength and stability of the alloy by forming a single BCC solid solution and precipitating coherent nanoprecipitations, which can relieve stress concentrations and prevent crack initiation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical performance, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanisms by which the refractory metals improve the properties of the alloy are not fully understood and require further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance of a lightweight high-entropy alloy with and without the addition of refractory metals such as Hf and Mo.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of refractory metals does not improve the mechanical performance, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance of the alloy, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract High entropy or compositionally complex alloys provide opportunities for optimization towards new high-temperature materials. Improvements in the equiatomic alloy Al 17 Co 17 Cr 17 Cu 17 Fe 17 Ni 17 (at.%) led to the base alloy for this work with the chemical composition Al 10 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6 (at.%). Characterization of the beneficial particle-strengthened microstructure by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and observation of good mechanical properties at elevated temperatures arose the need of accomplishing further optimization steps. For this purpose, the refractory metals hafnium and molybdenum were added in small amounts (0.5 and 1.0 at.% respectively) because of their well-known positive effects on mechanical properties of Ni-based superalloys. By correlation of microstructural examinations using SEM with tensile tests in the temperature range of room temperature up to 900 °C, conclusions could be drawn for further optimization steps. Keywords: HEA, high entropy alloys, compositionally complex alloys, mechanical characterization
